utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-97-25-T, the Prosecutor versus Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Witness, while you were detained at KP Dom, was there a group of detainees who worked?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To answer first, I forgot some notes in my hotel room, so could I have them? I'm too old, and if you're my age, I can't remember it all. So can we make a break? A break now or perhaps a bit later?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think, Ms. Kuo, the best idea is to take him through those particular matters. He can answer that question without notes, and if he has a particular problem, then we can deal with it later. Is there somebody from the Victim and Witnesses Section who can obtain these notes for him while we're going on?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can look into that. I'll certainly ask him specific questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And Witness, if there's a particular answer you don't know without your notes, you could let us know, but I think that you can probably answer most of these questions without them. Shall we try?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were there a group of detainees who worked? I won't ask you their names, but it's yes or no.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of work they did?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What kind of work did they do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went in groups. Metal workers, welders, they worked in workshop which was right next to the KP Dom. Others who were masons, they went out in groups. Carpenters, house painters, and workers who loaded and unloaded things, they were just manual workers. But all told, I could see them when they went out to lunch, when they went to the canteen, there were about 70, but the number varied. Sometimes there were less of them, times there were more. I can't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, you said you saw them going to the canteen. Do you know if they got different food from those who did not work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had an opportunity to see at the lunch with them because they had a line next to the window, those who went to have lunch there. They went together. And they had large bowls, three or four times larger than we had of that stew, if you can call it a stew, but it would be a sin to call it a stew because the food was bad. But they had three or four times more than we did, and two or three slices of bread, whereas we had only one, and we had only small bowls such as salad bowls. And men who worked there in the prison before, he told us that those were small salad bowls, perhaps one-third of a litre, perhaps even less than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, did a television crew ever come to visit KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it. I remember well. It was the 11th of August, and their team had two women and two men, if I remember well, and they spoke English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you see them filming?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you hear any conversation between any of the film crew and any of the prison officials?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conversation, I didn't. They spoke English. I couldn't understand, but they talked. There were two women in the team. One of them, those prisoners who were closer to the window, more aggressive, they looked through the window towards them in the yard, because that is in Room 11, it was on the ground floor. And one of those women, she unpacked a package of cigarettes and threw it in through the -- well, they're not bars, but there were some fittings on the window. And they -- she threw in 15 or 20 cigarettes, and people fought over those cigarettes. And the second woman - I hope I'm talking -- I'm speaking slowly enough and you can understand me - and the second woman with a camera recorded those scenes. At that time the guard commander, I think it was Rasevic, I saw him three or four times in the prison, he said - I understood him, he speaks our language - he said, "Lady, that's not how what we agreed about. Stop it, and you can go."

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask to have Exhibit P22, which is a videotape, now shown. The audio-visual director has a copy of the tape, but we would ask that the sound not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the KP Dom, the building. Husein Lojo, a French teacher to the right. That's the one. I don't know this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you recognise this room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the window. Ekrem Cemo to the -- on the left-hand side in a light suit but those were prisoners' clothes, the one on the end, and this is the prisoners' column as they walk into the canteen. I think that's it. Oh, no, sorry, in the room. This is the working groups room. Here they are having lunch. I saw them go in and the TV crew followed suit and recorded what we see now, this scene. I don't know this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Enough for the video tape, thank you. Witness, when you saw the pictures of people eating, were you able to see the portions of food they received?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the portions, yes. One could see those bowls because they were much larger, as I have already told you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were these the portions that the workers' group got or that the non-workers' group, detainees, received?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The workers' group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you have a chance to look at the woman who was the reporter who was standing in front of what you identified as Room 11?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure. I saw a woman who stood there and threw in the cigarettes and the other one was behind her, and you can't see her on the film.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The one you saw on the film, is that the one you said threw the cigarettes into Room 11?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a long time, eight years. Can't really remember, and I carry a burden of many years, so whether a woman was like this or like that, I don't know. There are women who look alike, but she looked like this one who threw in the cigarettes, and the other one was slimmer and taller, the one who was taking the shots. She was slightly taller and thinner than this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, while were you at KP Dom, did anyone ever tell you who the warden was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who told you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once, since you can see the canteen and across the compound's yard from my room, once, this gentleman, the warden, he was walking in front of the canteen, in front of the kitchen, and it's about 40 metres away. Yes, I'm sure it's that much. And so he was walking from there towards here and those prisoners who had arrived before me, they said that, "That's him, that's our warden, the prison warden." I saw him. I couldn't recognise him because I didn't know him from before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was the warden wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him. I saw him real well. He had an olive-grey/green uniform, the SMB uniform as they call it, the summer uniform, summer clothes, and he was bare-headed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did the detainees tell you his name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that's the prison warden, Milorad Krnojelac. I knew there was such a surname in our family, I don't know where, two or three places, I don't know where the man comes from. But the surname, yes, I heard it before. I knew it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, while were you at KP Dom, were detainees ever beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, in my room, I could not explain it to you before. People had been beaten, those in my room, but from my room at that time, nobody was taken out for beating while I was there. Only on three occasions I heard at night -- and I hope I'm speaking slowly and you can follow me. Three times I heard at night the beating and the cries of people for help. Across from my room, 11, I think on the second floor, how far is it? I don't know. Could be 10, 12, perhaps more metres, not too far, so that you could hear a typist typing on a typewriter, so I could hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say you could hear a typist, you don't mean there was actually a typewriter? You meant that it was that clear, right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once, I saw -- it was daytime, and I -- and the window was open because it was hot and I saw a woman walk across the room, and I guess it was a typist.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you heard the sounds of the beating, could you tell from Room 11 whether it was to the left or to the right of the entrance gate?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rooms were adjacent, the room to the side. Well, I didn't have all the devices to really measure where the sound came but it was across it to the left or to the right, but that's where it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: After the sounds of the beating, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On three occasions, I heard it. Once -- well, it happened sometimes at 10.00 until 12.00, and sometimes even later. And I heard three shots once, once five, and once seven. Five or four the second time but once I counted them, seven.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So there was a total of three occasions on which you heard shots, is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: After you heard those shots, did you hear anything else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, lights would go out. There were no lights. After that, I'd hear the sound of a vehicle. We call it TAM. It's a vehicle and I know its sound, a diesel one, and it would come to the door where the staff entered and the prisoners, and it would be there for about 15 or 20 minutes and then would go through the gate through which vehicles would go into the town, I mean freight vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What else would you hear?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard people being beaten and cry out, and that is horrible because when you hear screams, and you hear the blows, they were dull blows and we'd cover our ears so as not to hear because it was too -- we would run out into the farther room away and cover our ears and start talking loudly only so as not to hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you hear what direction this freight vehicle, this truck, went?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That truck went through the gate, what they call it one or two, I don't know, but the one which vehicles use. That is not the one that the guards and prisoners used. It couldn't go through that. But it was dark. All the lights were out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you hear the vehicle leave? Or first of all, from that entrance, where did the vehicle go?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I know where it went? Because it went through the gate so it's outside the compound. I don't know. Once --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to interrupt you, the witness said across the compound and this is not in the transcript, that the car went across the compound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It says because it went through the gate so it's outside the compound. You say in that particular answer, he said it went through the compound?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Across the compound through the gate. The witness says that's the same thing. And the witness said that, and it's not in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you better clear it up, Ms. Kuo. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With the assistance of the usher, I'd like the witness to be shown Exhibit P6.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, on this exhibit, are you able to identify the vehicle entrance that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Yes, I know this compound, and I went in by those gates very often down to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, maybe it would be better if we took the ground plan 6/1. It shows better, because this is a blown-up view of the KP Dom and one can't really see it here.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Except for this, except for this, Mr. Bakrac: That other one, the one with the drawing of the building, does not accurately show the courtyard because it has a wall going across, where clearly on the photographs it does not. So this may be, I think, the better one to deal with it. If there's any problem with it, then we'll try the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I apologise, I think there's -- it is not placed properly because perhaps it should be moved.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I agree with the lawyer. Will you move it so that one can see the yard? I can't read this. I can't see which is the administrative building. Ah, great, great. Very good. Building 1, building 2. This is the entrance. This is the staff entrance, here it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak into the microphone, please. Could the witness speak into the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just wait a minute, sir. Now, you've told us the entrance where the staff come in, and then you pointed at building number 1. What did you say there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that my finger doesn't get in the way, if you can see this. This is the staff entrance right here, that's the gate. This is my room, number 11. I hope you can see it. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. That's where the vehicle would come, to this gate, and that's it, to the right of me. Here it is. This is the bridge, a bit lower, across the Drina. I hope I've explained it enough. This is the road to the hospital as I'm showing it to you now. It is true. If the lawyer wasn't there and doesn't know, I know it, even though many years have past. I spent 35 years going down that road, that's how I earned my pension, taking the road towards the hospital. I hope I'm clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, you indicated the vehicle entrance which is on this exhibit to the right of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking from where I am, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you hear the vehicle go through the gate inside the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, you hear it when it comes close. When it goes in, then you can't hear it, but when it is in the courtyard, then you can hear it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, could you show us in the courtyard the path that you heard the car or the truck take?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here it would enter through the gate, naturally, and then move here to the personnel -- to the staff entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What would you hear when it got to the personnel --

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where they interrogated people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can we have that noted that that is outside the administration building, what we've been describing as the right-hand wing of the administration building, but inside the yard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What would you hear?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, when the vehicle arrived ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What would you hear when the vehicle arrived at that point?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The engine would be switched off when it arrived here. I didn't have a watch and I couldn't know, but about 20 minutes, about 20 minutes. It would be somewhere here. Then I could hear the engine being switched on again. The lights would be out, naturally, and with lowered lights, the vehicle would go out through the same gate that it entered through. And I guess, my guess is, that at that time they had nothing to bring in at night, especially since there were those shots, and I guess that at that time they were taking the bodies out, or they simply staged it in order to intimidate us. Can't be anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, were you able to identify any of the people who were taken out and beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time. Once I saw when they took away, I think, Rasim Reko. He was in another room, in another wing, not with me. I saw him walk across the compound once. He was taken to interrogation, and I couldn't see him as he was coming back. He was escorted by a guard, and I couldn't tell whether he was beaten and how much because he was dressed, and I didn't hear anything. I'm telling the truth as far as I know it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever see any injuries on a detainee?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who was that person, and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw with my eyes a man while I was in the isolation cell. That man's name is Habib Subasic. He was in isolation cell number 2, and we, the people who were in the isolation cells, were taking baths together. There was a common bathroom for the prisoners, so 15 people would normally take a shower, take a bath together. We would come in, and they would normally give us soap. I can't lie about this because they did. And up there, as far as I know, this was one of the best prisons, best KP Dom in Yugoslavia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I'm telling the truth. I don't want to sin. I don't want to take any sins on myself. And I saw Habib Subasic, this is a brother-in-law, his sister Zeka is married to him. I knew him personally. I knew both of them. They both worked in Foca. And as we were undressed, you know, normally we, the men, were taking a shower, so we were undressed, and I saw that he was all beaten up. His back was blue, turning into yellow, and I saw that. And I was horrified because I never saw anything like that before. And I asked him, "Habib, what is that?" And he said, "They beat me." I asked him, "Who beat you?" He said, "I don't know." And, you know, everyone is afraid of everyone else, and people would turn or mention names just to make it easier for themselves. They would talk on people just to make it easier on themselves, so he didn't tell me who beat him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he tell you whether he was beaten inside the KP Dom or outside?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In KP Dom, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, Habib Subasic is listed in Schedule B at 56.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, did any other detainees tell you they had been beaten while inside KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us their names and what they told you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll remember. I have it written down, but I will remember those who told me so. When I came in to Room 11, I found a lot of my acquaintances there because I worked in town and the industrial zone, so I got to know a lot of people through my work. I found Seljanci, Halim, there, an Albanian from Kosovo. He married a Bosnian woman, and he lived in a village towards -- somewhere around Tjentiste, Prejedjel. And since we knew each other from before, he was a construction worker, I -- he asked me, "How come you're here?" And I said, "Well, you know, fate. And how come you're here?" And he asked me whether I was tortured. I said, "Not so far." And he told me, "Well, they beat me terribly," and apparently after that he had to lie on his stomach for a week. He couldn't go to the canteen to eat, to eat there, and other people, other prisoners who were with him, were putting compresses on him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know approximately when this was, when he told you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when this took place because I came to KP Dom, I believe it was the 14th or the 15th of July, and they came before me, so I don't know when this had taken place. He didn't show me any bruises because by that time it already healed. I think it was in July, but I can't tell you exactly, so I better not talk of this further.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Seljanci, Halim, is listed in Schedule B at 51.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were there other detainees who told you they were beaten?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those that told me that they had been beaten.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know an Aziz Sajinovic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally. An economist, he worked in a bank, in a bank where I had my chequing account, and he would handle my account. I knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you what happened to him in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was very thin. He was a big man with a proper body build. He was very thin, and he was -- he had been beaten terribly. Three of his ribs were broken. This is what he told me. I don't know when he was taken in. Perhaps in May or something like that. But he told me that they put weight on him -- I'm sorry, that he was charged, and I can tell you what they charged him with. Since he was working with foreign currencies, in the bank, he was charged with stealing 30.000 -- embezzling 30.000 German Marks. And a Serbian lady who later fled to Belgrade apparently told on him and they beat him and asked that he confess about this embezzlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Aziz Sajinovic is listed in the indictment in paragraph 5.29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, do you know a Mustafa Vahida and what happened to him at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally know him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did he tell you what happened to him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know his father. I know his mother. I know where he was born. I know that he has a wife and two sons. I know where he lived in Cohodar Mahala. I know his house. Before I came there, they broke his jaw and knocked his teeth out. I don't know how many. I didn't ask him to show this to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was Mustafa Vahida's occupation?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, he was a policeman in SUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know his son, Dzemal?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you something. This is an error, Mustafa Vahida is the father of Dzemal Vahida. So there is an error there. Mustafa is the father of Dzemal Vahida. And I state this responsibly because I know his father personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was it Mustafa or Dzemal that was beaten, that you described his jaw was broken?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzemal's jaw, a policeman who used to work in SUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: So the person that you described having been beaten was Dzemal, the police officer, Dzemal Vahida?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, Dzemal Vahida is listed in Schedule C at 27.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if there were any land-mines inside the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if I can tell something not relating to KP Dom, another acquaintance of mine, he was beaten prior to coming to KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: No, no, just one moment, sir. Would you please answer the question that was asked of you? Do you know whether there were any land-mines inside the KP Dom? That's the question. Now, you can say yes or no to that.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is what I intended to say. I will tell you that now. Well, that was put in sometime in July, between 10th and 15th of July. This is when they put in mines because there was a rumour that escape was being planned. So Rasevic, Mitar, commander of guards -- I hope you can hear me well -- he came escorted by two policemen. He walked into my room, number 11, and we naturally lined up, it was in the evening hours before the counting time, and he warned us -- he gave us a warning, and he said, "Listen, people," and this is exactly what he said, "We had heard that some people are planning to escape. Don't play with your lives. We Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. put in mines." And this is not what I only heard. Everybody else heard it. He said, "Don't play with your lives because the mines are put in and you will get killed." Some other people said people are leaving, there is a panic among people, people are leaving and not coming back, and this is why people start feeling panicky. And after that, in the evening, and then every night, I think two or three mines exploded. They were activated right next to my room. There is a wall there and a fence, because this room where I was was at the end of the building. So we don't know whether a cat stepped on the mine, because there were some cats around there, or they activated it on purpose, just to mentally affect us. I don't know why they did it but I state firmly that mines were there. They were put in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness you stated yesterday that you were released from the KP Dom on the 31th of August, 1992. Could you tell us during the month and a half that you were at KP Dom, whether you lost weight, and if so, how much weight?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I lost a bit more than 17 kilograms.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And to this day, do you suffer from your experience at KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you describe to us in what way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can. For example, nightmares. They keep coming back. I keep dreaming about those scenes, screaming, beatings, people walking, thin as skeletons, and those who were above my room. Those, are the sights that I dream of. And even some names come to me, names that I had forgotten, and all of a sudden, at night, in my dreams, these names would come back to me and I would see these people, see their faces. And also, as I'm dreaming of this, sometimes I fall off my bed. I naturally sleep in a bed with my wife, and my wife, when this happens, my wife jumps up and says, "Well, what's wrong with you?" And I usually say, "I don't know, I don't know what's wrong with me." I fall off my bed. And I still have these nightmares to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honours, those are the Prosecution's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Cross-examination? Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I believe that I will be very brief as well but I do have a few questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. I'm Mihajlo Bakrac, one of the counsels for the accused, Milorad Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you testified about the early days of the conflict in the area where you lived. And since both of us speak the same language, and I will ask you to avoid the Trial Chamber warning us, I would ask you to wait for my question to be translated first and then give your reply. So, please, don't give your reply too quickly, in order to give the interpreters who participate in these proceedings, an opportunity to translate that.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You stated yesterday that on the 27th of April, your village was attacked. Was one of the -- were some of the houses destroyed, burned or destroyed in another way?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said no, and I can confirm this once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On 27th of April, did the Serb army come to your village?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Were any of the Muslims from your village killed, arrested or wounded on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you already gave one statement to the OTP investigators in 1995?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you stated that you continued living in the village, and that on 4th or 5th of July of 1992, you saw on television Muslims leaving Foca and being taken to Skopje, to Macedonia, and that then you decided to leave yourself?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it was on television. It was on the radio. However, it is true. We did watch the television because we had television; however, we didn't watch these scenes on television. We heard of it on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, it is irrelevant whether it was on the television or on the radio but what you stated was correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that a certain Veljko Lugonjic, while you were staying in Foca, and by your own account, as you were waiting for the bus to transport you to Skopje, that this individual asked you whether you had money for a bus ticket to Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This man was a secretary in the company where I had worked, and he offered to pay for the ticket, both for me and for my wife. And this took place while we were staying in Partisan.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that you stated that on the 31th of August, which was the day you were supposed to leave KP Dom on, Savo Todovic and a Serbian journalist named Todorovic came to the bus, and that Todovic said to the prisoners to state in front of the cameras how they were treated -- how they had been treated in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did any of the Muslims detainees talk to the journalists?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Who, who did?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tafro Fajik, an engineer. I was standing in the back so I didn't hear what they talked about. He probably said all the best, in order to save his life.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You stated that you were taken to Room 11. Can you please tell us, based on your memory, who did you find in Room 11?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you -- but I can't tell you everything. I left in my hotel room a list, you know the list that I made, but I can give you some names of those people that I knew personally, and I will give you those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, just the names that you can remember. You don't have to consult your list.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was a large room, Room 11, and I believe the warden knows about this. In fact, there were four rooms there and a living section of the room was in the middle and there were two rooms on the upper side and two rooms to the lower side but altogether, they comprise one single room. I knew the following people. I don't know if they are still alive. I don't know if where they are, if they are still alive. So I knew Hasan Lojo, Celik Hamid, Serif Hodzic. Hodzic Serif. Merkes Rasim, Rasim is his first name, that's correct. Rahman Adil, Soro Esed. These are the people that were in my room but just the dormitory that faced the backyard. And there was Lipa, Emir, there as well. I already said Soro. There was also Miralem Ramovic. I knew him personally, he was a driver. He used to work in my company. There was Dudic, Serif, and Dudic, Aziz. They were brothers, and I think they lived near Sukovci, somewhere around that area. I also -- Mr. Warden knows this man. There was Pasovic, Ismet, who used to work in KP Dom and who was retired now. He was 60 something. He slept next to me. We didn't have beds, but we had mattresses made out of thick sponge. We had blankets as well. There was Cankusic, Hasan, as well, and I remember that there was Soro, Suljo, as well. So these are the people from my room. And in the other room that was to the left, the other dormitory to the left, there was Cislja, Aziz; Muharem Vehabovic, who lived in Mahala. There was a man with the last name Babic. His father's name was Tahir Babic, and I don't know his first name, and he was a salesman. And there was a man called Mujo. I don't know his last name. He has a weird last name. And let me just try and remember the others that were there. I can't really remember it without a list. I know there was a man with a last name Muharem. I don't know his first name. And let me just see if I can remember who else was in that room. In other dormitories where there were fewer beds, there was Kovac, Dzafer; Dzemo, Vahida; Mandzo, Belmondo. I don't know his first name, but we used to call him Belmondo; that was his nickname. I don't know his first name. There was Demirovic, Sadam, a guy from Trebinje. Well, I don't know if I can remember without my list, the rest of the people in that room. And in the room on another side there was Taib Brahman. He was a salesman, worked in a store. Aziz Sahinovic was there. Hadzimusic, Anadziba's [phoen] younger son from Brod. I don't know his name. I can't remember. Oh, well, yes, there was Fehim Cimpo. He lived in a skyscraper and had an apartment across from Dr. Asima. And I don't think I can remember other names without my list. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Can you -- so these are the people that you found in Room 11 when you came there. Can you remember which date it was?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can remember. I came on the 15th. I believe it was the 15th. Yes, I spent seven days in Aladza prior to that, and I think it was the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Look, sir, you really must wait for a -- must pause after the question before you start your answer. I know you're very anxious to give your answer, but you are losing the interpreters, and if they lose what you say, then what you say is not recorded in the transcript. So, please, just wait, just wait a moment before you start your answer. And Mr. Bakrac, you are also coming in and asking the question whilst the interpretation of the answer is still running, so please, would you pause also.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, and I apologise to interpreters. I'll try not to create any further problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you stated that you came to that room on July 15th?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I came on the 15th of July to KP Dom, and then I spent seven days in isolation cells, and then I went to the room. So I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you came to Room 11 on the 22nd of July, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I guess so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So you found these people there, and they stayed in your room until you left the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have something I want to add. Not all of these people stayed there until I left because some of them were taken away prior to that, and I remember when they were taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you discussed the food in KP Dom, did you state that you were given one boiled, one boiled egg and some marmalade for breakfast?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We saw a videotape. Did you ever go into the working room?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which working room? Which working room do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I mean the room in which the workers' group stayed.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never went there. It wasn't possible. Nobody ever went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Then how could you recognise the room on the videotape?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you how. Because afterwards people told me that day, because that team had been announced, and they gave them fresh bed linen, gave them clean sheets, and the food was better. Secondly, they never allowed them to enter our room. They took them over there because they, I told you, they had better food and they had two slices of bread, and I saw them go in for lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But on the tape we also saw the canteen and a large number of persons eating there.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On the tape we saw the canteen and a large number of people having their meal there. We also saw some faces recorded on the tape on the ground floor in rooms. Were they all people of the workers' group?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the workers' group were those faces we saw in the canteen having lunch, and faces which are not shown are our faces which are inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd merely like to clarify something. When you spoke about those sounds, the sound of beatings that you heard, you told us that it usually happened between 10.00 and 12.00, but the transcript doesn't say whether it was in the morning or at night.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What's missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you said that you heard the sounds of beating between 10.00 and 12.00, was it by day or at night? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I told you in hours. I should have said between 2200 and 2400. That's when it happened, between 22.00 and 24.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said that on those occasions, lights were out in the compound. Was that a frequent occurrence?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it did happen, but not all that often, and then they would switch on their diesel generator. One could hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Re-examination, Ms. Kuo?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Just a clarification question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, when your village was attacked on the 27th of April, were there any Muslims actually inside the village when the soldiers arrived?

utterances.speaker: FWS-58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were. Some had gone, but the majority of them were there. Or rather, the 12 when they came, they left that same day, that is, and they left before. And we were left behind, 12 of us were left behind, that is, nine women and three men at that time. That's how many of us there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No other questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for giving your evidence. You may now leave, but please wait until the blinds are lowered so that you may leave without being seen by members of the public.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've finished what I had to do, don't have to come here any more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's right, sir. You may leave, and you are free to leave to return to your home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing, but perhaps you don't need it since you are not asking me to do that. You did not ask me how I left, when I started the first time with a bus on the 13th of August; and you didn't ask me that I was brought back from Niksic on that same day to the KP Dom when they took off 20 men and 34 were returned. You didn't ask me that, but I wanted to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Okay, sir. The parties have asked you all the questions they want answers from, so you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I hope I was clear enough. May punishment strike me if I did anything wrong, punishment by God or by this Court. Thank you very well

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, your next witness, Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next witness is FWS-35, and he has image alteration and a pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. The document with the pseudonym and the name of the witness headed "FWS-35" will be Exhibit P425, and it is under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in the document which is being shown to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down please, sir. Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, before you is Exhibit P425, and on it you should see FWS-35. Below that, is that your name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Below your name, is that your birth date?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You should understand that your name will not be used during these proceedings and you will be referred to only by that pseudonym. Underneath your birth date --

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Underneath your birth date there is the name of somebody and a pseudonym Z. If you refer to that person in the course of your testimony, could you please use the pseudonym Z instead of that person's name.

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, in 1992, which town did you live in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Foca.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: With whom did you live there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: My family.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you have --

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: My wife and three children.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What kind of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I worked in finance, in the field of finance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What level education did you have?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I graduated from the faculty of economics.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What ethnicity are you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: In 1992, were you politically active?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes, directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: In which party were you active?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Democratic party.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Would you -- how would you describe its platform? Was it a nationalistic party or different?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: That party was definitely not nationalistic. It wasn't a nationalistic party. It was a party with a democratic platform.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there a time when you could not live in your apartment but had to hide in the basement of your building in 1992?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Beginning of the latter half of April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Why did you feel it necessary to hide?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Because otherwise I would have been liquidated, or arrested at best.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did your family hide with you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: No, not with me, but yes, in a manner of speaking, even though they could lay their hands on my family.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Why were you afraid that you would be liquidated?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Because I was a Muslim, that is number one. Secondly, I was an educated man. Thirdly, as I've said, I dealt in finance. And four, because I belonged to the party that I belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Were there also Serbs that were hiding in the basement at that time with you, or was it only Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: In that basement before I hid there, as I told you, because I was afraid they might liquidate me, so in the beginning Serbs were hiding there. Later on, naturally, logically, I hid all by myself at the time that I told you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there a time when your family left the basement and went somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Where did your family go?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Why did they go there?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Because they thought that nothing could happen to them in a hospital. They believed that that was a place which was protected against everything that was going on. However, that was not the case, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did they go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: An ambulance car arrived. That is, a man whom I knew had sent that vehicle to get me out, because there was fighting in the town already and I could not leave normally, regularly, so that a neighbour, as my family was boarding that vehicle of a neighbour of mine, and he's a Serb, he asked me also to take his daughter along. There was one seat so I stayed behind, she joined them, and she left with my family to the hospital. So that I stayed there in the flat by the quirk of fate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was this still at the time when there was fighting in Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Not in the town itself. The fighting was not going on in the town itself but one could hear gunfire and there was shelling and, yes, you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know the reason why the daughter of your Serb neighbour also wanted to seek protection at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. I suppose she was afraid too, like my family. Why specifically? I have no idea but she asked me if she could come with us, and because there was one seat, then she took that seat that I thought would be mine. Of course, I agreed to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: After your family left, did you stay in the basement or did you go somewhere else in the building?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: At that time, I was in the basement and there were also Serbs with me, up to a certain time. When Foca was liberated, in inverted commas, then they left, I mean Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there at that -- do you remember the date when Foca was liberated, as you say?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: It happened between the 12 or 13 -- no, I'll be more specific, the beginning of the latter half of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: 1992, excuse me, interpreter's mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo, the transcript at line 2 of page 30, has used the word liberated without putting it in inverted commas. I think it is important that that is emphasised. It may be checked when the transcript -- when the tape is heard but it is an important qualification to what the witness was saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you explain what you mean when you say Foca was liberated? What act -- what happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: They considered it liberated, because they had taken over the power, and as of that moment, we became second-grade citizens, that is they began to harass, to arrest, to persecute, liquidate in floods and all the rest of it. That is, the word "liberation" is again indicated by the present name of the town Foca. It is now called Srbinje. That is, they even changed the name so that it would be linked to their nation, to their ethnic group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say "they," whom do you mean?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I mean Serbs, or rather extreme Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: After your family left the basement, was there a time when you stayed in someone's flat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Without using the person's name but a pseudonym if appropriate, whose flat did you stay in?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: For a short time, in person Z's flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was your relationship to Z?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: We were good neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of Z?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Why did you stay in his flat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Because my father called that person and told him that otherwise I would be arrested, that he promised he'd do that, and he also said that he wouldn't do it for me, but since it was my father who had called him from Sarajevo, he'd do it for him, for my father.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How many days did you stay in that person's flat?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Not very long.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know how many -- approximately how many days?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: A day or two, and I moved over to another flat then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: During the time that you stayed in that person's flat, did the name of Milorad Krnojelac ever come up?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you know Milorad Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Absolutely not. I knew the family. I mean, I knew the surname, I've heard about it, but otherwise, I didn't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did his name come up?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: His name came up in the following context. At the time when I was hiding in person Z's flat, I talked there with (redacted), and they are related. And after that, I asked, "What are you talking about?" And he said that (redacted) had been arrested and that he was in a concentration camp - and I'm going to use that term, "concentration camp," rather than prison or whatever, in my further testimony - and that (redacted) (redacted) had asked him if he could do something for the person that I've just mentioned, that is (redacted) because (redacted) had come to see (redacted) and asked him to intercede on his behalf. And he told me he'd call Krnojelac, and I asked him, "Who's that?" And he said that that was somebody, a teacher, who used to work (redacted) Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. (redacted), and he described him to me briefly: shortish, skinny. Do you want me to go on?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say "He described him to me," who is "he"? Who described Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Person Z, person Z.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How did person Z know Milorad Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And what did person Z say that he was going to do regarding Mr. Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: That he'd call. And he proceeded to do so immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Why was he calling Mr. Krnojelac? What was the purpose of the call?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: The purpose of the call was to help Enes Zekovic because the two of them, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just one moment. This Z that we have on the Exhibit 425, is that to be a witness in the case?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, but because this witness -- this witness has told us that he's a Serb, he was concerned about his identity being known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I'm concerned only so that we know how far the transcript has to be redacted, but a lot of what has been said, I think, will have to go out of the public version of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can perhaps -- it's a bit of a complicated story, and I think it's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I realise that but it may be that you are unable to obtain the story without this being disclosed. If there is a lot of it, it would be best if we went into private session for a short time so that the transcript doesn't, when it becomes public, have a whole series of redacted, redacted, redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That is probably the safer course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes. Well, then we will go into private -- will this take very long, this part of it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: No, it shouldn't. Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. Then we will go into private session in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are now back in public session. It seems hardly worthwhile asking another question at this stage, Ms. Kuo. We will adjourn now and resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Ms. Kuo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Witness, during the time that you were hiding, did any soldiers come looking? Did you encounter any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us where you were at that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: You mean during that encounter?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: On the staircase on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: There was three soldiers who were dressed in black. Two had also black berets with a characteristic sign, and a younger one had a black band, and something was written on it. I don't remember what. Those people had an accent, Serbian accent, which means that I did not know them at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did they say to you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: They asked me what was my ethnic background.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And what did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I told them I was a citizen of Yugoslavia and had Muslim religion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did they say anything to you then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: No, absolutely nothing. One of them, the older one, remained with the person Z, and the two soldiers walked behind me with a weapon pointed at me, and they asked me to go back to my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. I had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did anything happen to you after that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. We came to the apartment, and they very superficially searched the apartment. And I first initially thought that, you know, they in fact were not interested in searching the apartment, but they had much worse intentions. The younger one, who was about 24, told me that there was a war going on in Vukovar, and he told me to pick up an earth dish that was in the kitchen and to open it up, and when he saw that it was empty, we went back to the hallway. I was standing between the two of them in the kitchen. When we came back to the hallway, the two of them retreated to the same side. I was facing them, and one of them asked, "What should we do with him?" At that very moment, person Z walked in, basically running into my apartment, because I previously had an arrangement with him not to leave me alone, and at that moment he walked in and in a way he saved me from that situation, which was very unpleasant. So this was some kind of a threat. I don't know, a threat of potential shooting or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: When you say he saved you, in what way did he save you?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Well, by his own presence he saved me. At that moment when they were wondering what to do with me, he showed up at that very moment, and naturally they couldn't shoot. However, they had the position from which they could shoot at me. It was a very characteristic, very typical position that they had at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What did those soldiers do then?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: We left the apartment together, and person Z told me that since there were three individuals there, two of them took me to my apartment, and the older one remained with person Z, and person Z later on told me that this individual had told him that they were not allowed to be friendly with Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you encounter soldiers or did soldiers come back?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. Around 2.00 a.m., one person who happened -- I went to my apartment by chance. I went there to take a shower. And a person whose name I do not wish to mention because I'm very grateful to this person -- this person is not alive any more but I still do not wish to mention this person's name. So this person called me and said, "Run away, they will cut your throat." When I asked this person who, the person just repeated, "Run. They will cut your throat." And at that moment, since I was dressed, I went immediately down to the basement. And as soon as I walked into the basement, I heard terrible noise. Since the door was locked and the person Z, based on our prior agreement, had the key, unfortunately, he had a wrong key. They said, "Open up or we will shoot." This person went back to his apartment, took a right key and came back. I recognised the voice of the younger soldier who had been in my apartment that very day, and this person asked, "Where is that dark man?" The person Z asked, "Which one?" The soldier said, "Where is that balija?" And I could hear other voices that I could recognise, which means that those were local Chetniks. There was a group of about 10 people there, and they mentioned my name. So this young person, this young soldier, who had been in my apartment previously that day, said that he would be my judge and my executioner. They went with person Z. The person Z walked in front of them, and this is what I'd been told by this person. They pointed rifles into his back. They walked to my apartment. I heard from the basement Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. terrible noise, which means that they broke into my apartment and searched it. At that very moment, another person went down to the basement. I know this person's nickname, which was Zelja, and this person went down to the basement to search it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Excuse me, I'm going to interrupt you there. How -- did you see this person Zelja when he came down to the basement?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: No, no. I wouldn't be alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: How do you know it was him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Mother of a girl who I let go to the hospital instead of me was together with me in the basement, so she was the one who told me. She covered me with blankets and then those women sat on me. She told me, "Don't worry, I will go out." She went, a bottle of brandy, and she went out into the hallway which was in front of the basement and she started towards this person, towards Zelja as he was coming down the stairs. And then she asked him what he wanted. And he replied that he wanted to search the basement. She told him there were only women and children there. He kept insisting on doing that. She recognised his voice and then she told him, "Is that, you, Zelja?" and cursed his mother and told him, "If you come in, I will call Pero Elez," because Pero Elez was a high-ranking individual. So she threatened him with his name, and then they had a friendly chat and perhaps had a drink or two. And in the end, he did not go into the basement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you hear what happened -- what the other people were doing, the ones who went upstairs with person Z?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Earlier you said that you heard the sound of your apartment being broken into. From that point on, did you hear what those people did or said?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: In my apartment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Either in your apartment or outside your apartment.

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Well, so they actually searched the apartment. And as they were coming back from the apartment, person Z recognised Krnojelac's brothers and asked them, "Are you Milorad's relatives?" And then they had a friendly chat there, which means that he did not recognise them at that moment, because they went to my apartment and the weapons were pointed at him. And after they searched it, they went downstairs and as they were coming out of the building, this is where he asked them, are you those and those and then they had had a very simple, friendly chat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you actually hear Z ask the question, "Are you Milorad's relatives?"

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you hear a response?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Well, yes. After that, well, they were talking. They continued talking, which means that the answer was affirmative. I can't remember right now whether it was an explicit "yes". However, they had a very natural conversation with typical questions, which indicated they had known each other.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did person Z tell you afterwards who those two people were, those two relatives of Milorad?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. Person Z told me that it was those individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Who were they? What did person Z tell you? You're allowed to use their names if he told you the names.

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I don't know the names. I can't remember. I think that in my first statement I did give the first names. However, he -- I said that they were Milorad's sons. And the names are in the statement, the first names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: If I showed you a copy of your first statement, would that help you remember?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: I'll ask the usher to hand the ID, the document ID 108A to the witness and direct the witness to page 5.

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes, that's the statement I gave. That's right, the names are here. The first one mentioned I know because he had a cafe bar and I could describe him, which means that I knew him superficially from before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Spomenko Krnojelac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And the other son?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Bozidar.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Perhaps by sight.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Z or this woman who talked to Zelja tell you whether they were able to recognise or to see the faces of the people that they talked to, or were they covered?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Based on my assumption and based on what I described to you, it is likely that those people had stockings on their faces because it was, it was in the early days or the first day when they entered, in inverted commas, the town. So it would be logical for them to be covered because they were not sure of the outcome, so it is likely that they had stockings over their faces. That's my assumption, but this is also what I've heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: The three soldiers you did see earlier that day, did they have stockings over their faces?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did your family return at some point?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And did you continue to hide?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes, the whole time until St. Vitus's day, 28th of June, which is when I left Foca, I think, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Where did you hide after your family came back?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: In my apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was there a specific place in your apartment that you hid?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. The most visible location in the kitchen, under the sink. It was a great risk, and there was a great likelihood of them finding me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: In fact, did soldiers continue looking for you during that time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion Zoran Vukovic came with another man. They came into the apartment. They searched it. They inquired as to my whereabouts and said that it was -- I was making a grave error of not being there, because officially I was in Montenegro. I simply tried to detract attention from my family and my apartment. And then at the end he asked for a glass of water, which means that he and I were about ten centimetres apart.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: But you were hidden, right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. I was under the sink, in the cabinet under the sink.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Now, witness you said you were officially in Montenegro. What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Not officially, not, not -- not on business, simply that I fled into Montenegro because the war was going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Was that true?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: No, absolutely no. I was in the apartment, or rather, in the apartment building. I was hiding there the entire time. This was simply a tactical move on my part. And my wife spread this rumour around through the neighbours because we know that they had been looking for me very actively.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: While you were hiding, did you ever hear any broadcasts of a speech by Miroslav Stanic?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Can you tell us who Miroslav Stanic was during this time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Chairman of the SDS, and later on chairman of the SDS Crisis Staff. We cooperated politically as far as was possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Where was the speech being broadcast?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Behind my apartment building in the so-called JNA hall there was a radio station, and there were loudspeakers so that this broadcast was -- could be heard really well. Two things that I remember very vividly and which I can quote is that, "Hodza's voice will not be heard in Foca any more," and that "Circumcised Muslim children will not walk around the town any more." So these two statements, in addition to war conditions and so on, is something that I remember quite vividly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said "hodza's voice." Could you explain what you meant by that? It may not be clear.

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Which means that Muslim -- Islam religion would not be present there any more, and also that there wouldn't be any more Muslim children there, because they had mentioned circumcised Muslim children, which means that all those children would be destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you recognise Miroslav Stanic's voice, or was he announced or introduced?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I gave statements to the same radio station before the war. I know this individual personally because he was announced as the chairman of the Crisis Staff. They announced his name, his first name and his last name, but I also recognised his voice.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Approximately when did you hear this announcement? You can just tell us the month and approximately when.

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: I heard the broadcast when my family was in the apartment. My family returned around the 25th of April, which means -- let me just put it in a time frame. So this means that that probably was late April, early May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you ever hear any other announcements placing restrictions on the movement of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Across from my apartment building there was a police vehicle which announced information through a loudspeaker, which means that that car would stop every 100 or 200 metres in order to cover a certain area and announce certain information. One of the information announced was that Muslim males between 18 and 65 years were not allowed to leave town, and also, they were not allowed to meet together in Muslim houses. I heard this loud and clear. There were two individuals in that vehicle wearing old, former Yugoslav police uniforms, and this is the announcement I had heard because my balcony was open and the distance was quite little, quite short between where I was standing and this vehicle. And then this vehicle continued driving towards the market. This is what I observed. So as I said, this was a police vehicle with policemen in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: And to clarify, this was civil police, not military; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes, civil police of the former Yugoslavia. So the vehicle belonged to the police of the former Yugoslavia, and the policemen wore typical uniforms that policemen of the former Yugoslavia had.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Now, you said that one of the announcements was that Muslim men between 18 and 65 were not allowed to leave town. Was there any restriction on their ability to walk about inside the town?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Well, yes, there was a limitation on their movement. They were not -- their ability to move around the town was limited. So one could see only women in the stores; one couldn't see any men in the store. And I could see this because I was standing at a very good location with -- a high traffic location, so I could observe this very clearly. The only individual adult male that I saw moving around was very shortly thereafter arrested and went to prison, and if needed, I can state the name of this individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: It's not necessary at this point, Witness. Did your wife go to work during this time?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: After my return from Sarajevo, because I went to Sarajevo for the weekend and then returned to Foca, so my wife one or two days later went to work. And after that, she was told that she was not desirable there at the office.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: You said you went to Sarajevo. I think we need to clarify your time period. When was it that your wife was told she was not needed at work?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. I can say this. If Monday, in 1992, was the 6th, we can verify this, or, rather, you can verify this. So 8th or 9th of April of 1992, this is what she was told, that she was not wanted in the office because she was my wife.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Is your wife Muslim?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: What ethnicity is she?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: She is orthodox, which means a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Could you tell us when you finally left Foca? You said St. Vitus's Day. Could you tell us how you left Foca?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: With the assistance of a person whose name I do not wish to mention because this person is not alive any more. So this person helped me leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Did you obtain a permit to leave?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KUO
utterances.text: Perhaps you could clarify, if you know this. If you had spread the rumour that you were already not in town, how was it that you were able to secure a permit to leave? Do you know the answer to that?

utterances.speaker: FWS-35
